land.text: Haryana, eastern Punjab and northern Rajasthan, Kushan land until the Yaudheya blow

predecessors.note: Yaudheya page: Majumdar puts a blow to the Kushans at 'approximately 180 CE', after which they ceased to be present in Eastern Punjab. The infobox says 'Preceded by the Kuru Kingdom'. Cliopatria's Eastern Kushan shapes of 238-269 cover 818 of the 837 Yaudheya cells. Kushan Empire page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Around 270 their territories on the Gangetic plain became independent under local dynasties such as the Yaudheyas'.

capitals.name: Rohtak
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Rohtak'. Altekar describes three republics, one centred on Rohtak, a second on northern Pancala (Bahudhanyaka) and a third in northern Rajputana; Cliopatria draws one.

correction.text: the Yaudheya core around Rohtak (infobox capital), 44 cells: the whole of the Cliopatria 306 shape lies inside the Kushan Empire (200-225), Eastern Kushan (238-269) and Western Satrap shapes of these years, so no cell of it is uncontested

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 200-269, cut on 2026-10-19 (reviewer). Before: Cliopatria's 306 shape (837 cells) carried back to 200-305. It lies wholly inside neighbours' Cliopatria shapes until 269 (Kushan Empire 184/215/224 shapes: 818 cells; Eastern Kushans 238, 260: 818 cells; Western Satraps 224/260: 19 cells; uncontested cells 0), and the neighbours' dossiers (kushan-empire, eastern-kushans, western-satraps, all verdict ok) keep those shapes. The Yaudheya page (opened) has the Yaudheyas dealing the Kushans a blow c. 180 and ruling independently 'from the beginning of the 3rd century'; the Kushan Empire page (opened 2026-10-19) has 'Around 270 their territories on the Gangetic plain became independent under local dynasties such as the Yaudheyas'. The pages disagree and the neighbours' shapes follow the later one, so only the Rohtak core (60 km, 44 cells, the Yaudheya page's capital) is kept from 200 to mark the birth, and it stays an admitted overlap; the full country follows in 270-305. Routing: kushan-empire (184-224 shapes) and eastern-kushans (238-269) should cut Haryana if the Yaudheya page's early date is preferred.

correction.text: Cliopatria's Yaudheya 306 shape without the 230 cells that the Western Satraps' 270 shape holds: Haryana, the eastern Punjab, Uttarakhand and northern Rajasthan between the Sutlej and the Jumna

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 270-305 (reviewer repair 2026-10-19): 607 of the 837 cells of the 306 shape. Kushan Empire page: 'Around 270 their territories on the Gangetic plain became independent under local dynasties such as the Yaudheyas'; the Eastern Kushans' own 270 shape (eastern-kushans_270) leaves the Yaudheya cells, while the Western Satraps' 270 shape (842,057 km2) still holds 230 of them until western-satraps /ledger/11 (306) gives them to the Yaudheyas. The Yaudheya page gives no area.

220,128 km2 (837 cells): Haryana 100%, Indian Punjab 56%, Rajasthan 29%, Uttarakhand 23%, a little Uttar Pradesh and Himachal. The page: coins 'extended from Saharanpur in the east to Bahavalpur in the west' (Altekar), 'large hoards between the Sutlej and the Jumna', a republic centred on Rohtak, one on northern Pancala and one in northern Rajputana (the Bijayagarh pillar, Bharatpur district). The shape covers that block. The page gives no area. Gains 230 cells from the Western Satraps' shape in 306 (western-satraps /ledger/11 loses them; ledger gain below).

220,729 km2, same outline. Samudragupta page: the Yaudheyas ruled between the Sutlej and Yamuna after the Kushans and 'seem to have become Samudragupta's tributaries'; Yaudheya page: 'the payment of all tributes' listed in the Allahabad Pillar, without armed resistance. Cliopatria keeps the republic as a separate shape; the tribute is drawn as a Gupta vassal event (gupta-empire, 347-378).

220,729 km2, same outline. 'This particular period marked the gradual disintegration of the Yaudheya republic.' Cliopatria ends the shape in 377 and adds it to the Gupta in 378; the page says only that the republic was disestablished in the 4th century CE.

region.text: the Yaudheya core around Rohtak, the capital of the infobox

ledger.note: c. 200: the Yaudheyas rule themselves between the Sutlej and the Jumna after the Kushan blow. Yaudheya page: 'in approximately 180 CE' (Majumdar) the Yaudheyas and allied janapadas dealt a blow to the Kushans, after which the Kushans ceased to be present in Eastern Punjab; post-Kushan coins with 3rd- or 4th-century legends mark independent rule from the beginning of the 3rd century (the page's wording). The year is the page's 'beginning of the 3rd century'; the land is Altekar's coin-hoard area as drawn in Cliopatria's 306 shape. Repair 2026-10-19: the birth is drawn at the Rohtak core only (60 km), because the rest of the Cliopatria 306 shape lies inside the Kushan shapes of 200-269 (see keyframe yaudheya-republic_200); the counterpart is kushan-empire (the Kushan state of 200; eastern-kushans begins in 226).

Kushan Empire page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Around 270 their territories on the Gangetic plain became independent under local dynasties such as the Yaudheyas.' Cliopatria's Eastern Kushans drop 818 Yaudheya cells in 270 (eastern-kushans /ledger/4 records the loss to 'nobody', 270). The year is the page's; the land is the Cliopatria 306 shape, my reading. Added 2026-10-19 on the reviewer's finding (the 200-305 keyframe overlapped the Kushan shapes).

region.text: the 230 cells of Rajasthan and Haryana that Cliopatria's Western Satraps shape holds until 305

ledger.note: c. 306: the Yaudheyas take 230 cells from the Western Satraps' shape. Cliopatria's Yaudheya row begins in 306 and the Western Satraps shape drops those cells in the same year (western-satraps /ledger/11). Yaudheya page: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription (c. 150) says he 'by force destroyed the Yaudheyas who were loath to submit' and Cunningham saw a plundering raid, not rule; the page dates no later retreat. The year is Cliopatria's. Added 2026-10-19 on the reviewer's finding.

c. 347: the Yaudheyas become Samudragupta's tributaries. Samudragupta page: the Yaudheyas 'seem to have become Samudragupta's tributaries'; the Yaudheya page, on the Allahabad Pillar: their rule was 'propitiated with the payment of all tributes', without armed resistance (Upinder Singh: no troops supplied). The year is bridged from Samudragupta's reign (c. 335-375) and the Cliopatria Gupta jump of 347; mirrors gupta-empire /ledger (vassal_start 347). Added 2026-10-19 on the reviewer's finding.

c. 377: the tribute ends with the state: the Gupta shape absorbs the republic (gupta-empire /ledger gain and vassal_end, 378). The Chandragupta II page (opened 2026-10-19) does not mention the Yaudheyas, and no page dates the end. Added 2026-10-19.

region.text: the Yaudheya country between the Sutlej and the Jumna, from Saharanpur in the east to Bahawalpur in the west

ledger.note: c. 377: the Yaudheya republic ends in the Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire page lists 'Yaudheya' among the empire's predecessors; the Yaudheya page gives 'Disestablished: 4th century CE' and the Gupta Empire as successor in its infobox. Neither dates the end: Cliopatria ends its shape in 377 and adds exactly its 840 cells to the Gupta in 378.

wars.name: Yaudheya-Kushan struggle

zones.text: Eastern Punjab, Haryana and northern Rajasthan

wars.outcome: The Yaudheyas and allied janapadas dealt a blow to the Kushans c. 180 CE, after which the Kushans ceased to be present in Eastern Punjab; the Kushans are said to have annexed the Yaudheyas earlier (the Maaseno coins).
wars.note: Years are the researcher's bridge around 'approximately 180 CE'. Repair 2026-10-19: belligerent kushan-empire (was eastern-kushans, which begins in 226); zone from the Kushan Empire shape of 184-214.

wars.name: Samudragupta's subjugation of the Yaudheyas
wars.outcome: The Allahabad Pillar lists the Yaudheyas among the tributaries; they paid tribute without armed resistance, and Upinder Singh notes no troops were supplied.
wars.note: Samudragupta's reign is c. 335-375; the page dates no campaign.

certainty.note: The pages give coin-hoard areas (Saharanpur to Bahawalpur, Sutlej to Jumna), no frontier line; the whole life is soft.

notes:
Cliopatria row: one row, 306-377, no split. The dossier starts the republic in 200 (the page: independent rule from the beginning of the 3rd century), not 306: the 306 shape is carried back, which overlaps the Eastern Kushans' 238-269 shapes (818 of 837 cells) and the Western Satraps' 270-305 shape (230 cells). If the Kushan or Satrap groups keep those shapes, the keyframe yaudheya-republic_200 may be cut to 270-305.
Page budget: 1 of 1-2 (Yaudheya); the Samudragupta and Gupta Empire pages (opened for the Gupta dossier) are cited for the tribute and the successor.
Unsettled: (1) no page dates the end; 377 is Cliopatria's (the Gupta 378 shape equals the 358 shape plus this one); (2) the page's infobox 'Established: 5th century BCE' and 'Preceded by the Kuru Kingdom' mean the Yaudheyas are far older than this dossier: Cliopatria has no earlier shape and none of the pages draws one; (3) the tributary status under Samudragupta is recorded on the Gupta side (vassal_start/vassal_end); the dates are conf 1. (4) Johiyawar, Agroha, the Bahudhanyaka country and Bahawalpur are not in the gazetteer by those names.
Gazetteer names needed: Bahudhanyaka, Agroha (places) for the northern Pancala republic; none is used as a region key here.

REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after review): (1) The 200 founding and the predecessor now name kushan-empire (the Kushan state of 200; eastern-kushans begins in 226). (2) Keyframe 200-305 is cut: the Cliopatria 306 shape lies wholly inside the Kushan Empire (200-225), Eastern Kushan (238-269) and Western Satrap shapes (0 uncontested cells before 270; 607 cells from 270 because eastern-kushans_270 leaves them and the Western Satraps keep 230 until 306). The neighbours keep their shapes, so the Yaudheya keep a 60 km Rohtak core from 200 (44 cells, an admitted overlap that marks the birth the Yaudheya page gives), the full country from 270 (Kushan Empire page: independent 'around 270 ... under local dynasties such as the Yaudheyas') and 230 more cells in 306 from the Western Satraps. The pages disagree: the Yaudheya page says independence from the beginning of the 3rd century and a Kushan blow c. 180, the Kushan Empire page says 270; Cliopatria draws Kushan, then Eastern Kushan, rule over Haryana until 269. (3) Vassalage of Samudragupta: vassal_start 347 and vassal_end 377 with gupta-empire (the Gupta side closes at 378). (4) The war against Rudradaman (c. 145-150, Junagadh inscription: 'by force destroyed the Yaudheyas who were loath to submit'; Cunningham: a plundering expedition) was dropped from wars[] because it lies before the state's start; it remains in the 306 gain note. (5) Page tried for the end year: Chandragupta II (does not mention the Yaudheyas); the 377 end stays Cliopatria's at confidence 1. Counterpart routing: eastern-kushans /ledger/4 (270 loss to nobody) could name yaudheya-republic for the Haryana part.
